::: {.notes}
Huang et al. evaluated 300 prompts across five equally sized domains with Qwen3.8-27B. Each prompt required several strings on specified surfaces. The bounded word error rate compares the transcription of each target in its clearest frame with the reference text. The scene score is the fraction of 20 scene and motion requirements met per prompt. Both metrics range from zero to one. Table 1 separates readable lettering from visual adherence. [VTR-Bench · Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01499v1#S4.T1).

The duration diagram applies the API reference parameter duration. A request with 10 seconds of input video leaves at most 20 seconds for output. Across the reference clips the input limit is 15 seconds. The three rows are calculated examples of the documented limit.

The specification table follows the 19 October 2026 workbook. The date shown is the Alibaba Cloud blog date adopted by the workbook. The workbook records conflicting third-party release dates and an API preview status.

The workbook reports that Model Studio offers standard and Prime IDs with six tasks. This describes the documented Model Studio interface; other providers can expose a narrower subset. Prompt expansion is external LLM preprocessing, not a disclosed component of Wan3's generator. The Prime acceleration method is not published, so do not infer distillation or a smaller backbone. Prior Wan versions do not establish Wan3 architecture.

The 30-second limit is for a single output; when video is supplied, input plus output must remain within 30 seconds. The reference limit is 20 total files, subject to separate per-modality and duration limits. Editing and extension are selected using the reference video and prompt intent. A file or webpage can trigger additional preprocessing. The Apache-2.0 statement concerns the repository README; the audit found no checkpoints or separately published Wan3 weight licence.

:::
